entries.name: MVC (Model-View-Controller)
entries.reason: Model increment, Controller click and View render each occur once and demonstrate separate MVC responsibilities; sharing their DATA would erase the boundary, while a copied model-reference template is longer than the two short fields.

entries.name: MVP (Model-View-Presenter)
entries.reason: Presenter mutates the model and then updates Screen through its second input value. No repeated action is removable; converting show/value or click/delta to the first position would target different DATA fields.

entries.name: MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel)
entries.reason: The model update and subscribed screen update are distinct effects. value is not the first DATA field in either component, so named actuals remain; a template costs more than the two short declarations.

entries.name: Flux / Redux
entries.reason: Use positional state and delta for the visibly ordered Reducer DATA. Reducer invocation, current-store update and the saved intermediate state remain; no helper is hidden.
entries.before_code:
Reducer:
    int: state
    int: delta
    return: int
    reduce:
        return: state + delta

Store:
    int: state 0
    int: delta
    dispatch:
        node\state := Reducer\reduce(state := node\state; delta := delta)

Demo:
    return: int
    run:
        Store\state := 0
        Store\dispatch(delta := 2)
        int: previous Store\state
        Store\dispatch(delta := 3)
        return: previous * 10 + Store\state
entries.after_code:
Reducer:
    int: state
    int: delta
    return: int
    reduce:
        return: state + delta

Store:
    int: state 0
    int: delta
    dispatch:
        node\state := Reducer\reduce(node\state; delta)

Demo:
    return: int
    run:
        Store\state := 0
        Store\dispatch(delta := 2)
        int: previous Store\state
        Store\dispatch(delta := 3)
        return: previous * 10 + Store\state

entries.name: Layered Architecture
entries.reason: Use positional quantity in Application.total and Presentation.handle; each DATA visibly has that sole input. All three layers and their calls remain in the full listing.
entries.before_code:
Data:
    return: int
    price:
        return: 10

Application:
    int: quantity
    return: int
    total:
        return: quantity * Data\price()

Presentation:
    int: quantity
    return: int
    handle:
        return: Application\total(quantity := quantity)
    demo:
        return: handle(quantity := 3)
entries.after_code:
Data:
    return: int
    price:
        return: 10

Application:
    int: quantity
    return: int
    total:
        return: quantity * Data\price()

Presentation:
    int: quantity
    return: int

        return: Application\total(quantity)
    demo:

entries.name: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)
entries.reason: Use the visible Core input order quantity, price for both calls. Both distinct adapters and the two quotations remain; a helper or common quantity local is longer than this positional form.
entries.before_code:
Adapters:
    return: int
    memory:
        return: 10
    alternate:
        return: 12

Core:
    int: quantity
    @: price
    return: int
    quote:
        return: quantity * price()
    demo:
        return: quote(quantity := 2; price := Adapters\memory) + quote(quantity := 2; price := Adapters\alternate)
entries.after_code:
Adapters:
    return: int
    memory:
        return: 10
    alternate:
        return: 12

Core:
    int: quantity
    @: price
    return: int
    quote:
        return: quantity * price()
    demo:
        return: quote(2; Adapters\memory) + quote(2; Adapters\alternate)

entries.name: Clean Architecture
entries.reason: Use visible input order income, expense for Policy and income, expense, output for UseCase. Keep the external output(decision := ...) contract and both complete Policy/Presenter implementations.
entries.before_code:
Policy:
    int: income
    int: expense
    return: int
    eligible:
        return: income - expense >= 30

Presenter:
    int: decision
    return: int
    render:
        if: decision != 0
            return: 200
        return: 422

UseCase:
    int: income
    int: expense
    @: output
    return: int
    execute:
        return: output(decision := Policy\eligible(income := income; expense := expense))
    demo:
        return: execute(income := 100; expense := 60; output := Presenter\render)
entries.after_code:
Policy:
    int: income
    int: expense
    return: int
    eligible:
        return: income - expense >= 30

Presenter:
    int: decision
    return: int
    render:
        if: decision != 0
            return: 200
        return: 422

UseCase:
    int: income
    int: expense
    @: output
    return: int
    execute:
        return: output(decision := Policy\eligible(income; expense))
    demo:
        return: execute(100; 60; Presenter\render)

entries.name: Onion Architecture
entries.reason: Use the visible submit input order order, save. Keep the named order actual on the saved callback because Repository has last before order; identity and save-before-total behavior remain.
entries.before_code:
Order:
    int: quantity 3
    int: price 10
    return: int
    total:
        return: quantity * price

Repository:
    @: last 0
    @: order
    save:
        node\last := order

Application:
    @: order
    @: save
    return: int
    submit:
        save(order := order)
        return: order\total()
    demo:
        return: submit(order := Order; save := Repository\save)
entries.after_code:
Order:
    int: quantity 3
    int: price 10
    return: int
    total:
        return: quantity * price

Repository:
    @: last 0
    @: order
    save:
        node\last := order

Application:
    @: order
    @: save
    return: int
    submit:
        save(order := order)
        return: order\total()
    demo:
        return: submit(Order; Repository\save)

entries.name: Microservices
entries.reason: The only external exchange is one HTTP request with named endpoint, route and quantity. Its DATA order is not declared locally, and there is no repeated request to factor without changing the protocol.

entries.name: Event-Driven Architecture
entries.reason: Two sends have different destinations and must both occur. sendEvent is an external port with no local positional DATA; adding a wrapper or destination loop exceeds the two calls.

entries.name: CQRS
entries.reason: Reuse the existing ReadMessage.query method for the apply result. The state write still occurs before the read; query itself remains read-only and cannot dispatch a command.
entries.before_code:
WriteMessage:
    int: balance 0
    int: amount
    @: transport
    add:
        throws: Amount
        if: amount < 0
            throw: Amount()
        node\balance += amount
        node\transport\publish(node\balance)

ReadMessage:
    int: visible 0
    int: snapshot
    return: int
    apply:
        node\visible := snapshot
        return: node\visible
    query:
        return: node\visible
entries.after_code:
WriteMessage:
    int: balance 0
    int: amount
    @: transport
    add:
        throws: Amount
        if: amount < 0
            throw: Amount()
        node\balance += amount
        node\transport\publish(node\balance)

ReadMessage:
    int: visible 0
    int: snapshot
    return: int
    apply:
        node\visible := snapshot
        return: query()
    query:
        return: node\visible

entries.name: Event Sourcing
entries.reason: Balance has one replay loop and append one optimistic store operation. No duplicate loop exists within this example; importing a reducer would move visible implementation work outside the compared boundary.

entries.name: Pipe and Filter
entries.reason: Use the sole visible value position for pipeline(-3). The normalize/double/offset stages and measured PipeLibrary usage remain unchanged.
entries.before_code:
Filters:
    int: value
    return: int
    normalize:
        if: value < 0
            return: -value
        return: value
    double:
        return: value * 2
    offset:
        return: value + 1
    pipeline:
        import: PipeLibrary
        return: value pipe normalize double offset
    demo:
        return: pipeline(value := -3)
entries.after_code:
Filters:
    int: value
    return: int
    normalize:
        if: value < 0
            return: -value
        return: value
    double:
        return: value * 2
    offset:
        return: value + 1
    pipeline:
        import: PipeLibrary
        return: value pipe normalize double offset
    demo:
        return: pipeline(-3)

entries.name: Blackboard
entries.reason: normalize and derive have different readiness conditions and writes. Their shared success/failure return shape is too small to repay a complete helper with dynamic target/value setup; the retrying scheduler remains.

entries.name: Microkernel / Plug-in
entries.reason: Set the demo-local value to 5 once and reuse ordinary autofill for both execute() calls. Kernel.value has no default, Plugins receive the same explicit value, and both install operations and plugin bodies remain.
entries.before_code:
Plugins:
    int: value
    return: int
    twice:
        return: value * 2
    thrice:
        return: value * 3

Kernel:
    @: extension Plugins\twice
    @: implementation
    int: value
    return: int
    install:
        node\extension := implementation
        return: 1
    execute:
        return: node\extension(value := value)
    demo:
        install(implementation := Plugins\twice)
        int: first execute(value := 5)
        install(implementation := Plugins\thrice)
        return: first + execute(value := 5)
entries.after_code:
Plugins:
    int: value
    return: int
    twice:
        return: value * 2
    thrice:
        return: value * 3

Kernel:
    @: extension Plugins\twice
    @: implementation
    int: value
    return: int
    install:
        node\extension := implementation
        return: 1
    execute:
        return: node\extension(value := value)
    demo:
        int: value 5
        install(implementation := Plugins\twice)
        int: first execute()
        install(implementation := Plugins\thrice)
        return: first + execute()

entries.name: Repository
entries.reason: This client already reuses the measured FindLibrary operand. Factoring its one call adds code; removing the adjacent implementation cost would violate the comparison boundary.

entries.name: Unit of Work
entries.reason: writeAll is already the shared transaction body. The loop must preserve dirty entries on failure and clear only after a successful atomic call; a collection callback adds a wrapper rather than removes duplicate work.

entries.name: Data Mapper
entries.reason: Loading copies the complete id/cents template once; saving writes a row once. A common projection helper would need both different source layouts and would not shorten the complete mapper.

entries.name: Active Record
entries.reason: debit validation/update and save are separate operations with different effects. Their repeated node qualifier is not repeated application logic, and both id and cents must remain.

entries.name: Table Data Gateway
entries.reason: SELECT and UPDATE have different SQL strings, results and parameter orders. A shared database wrapper would retain both queries and add an extra callable; no smaller complete variant was established.

entries.name: Row Data Gateway
entries.reason: One UPDATE operation already contains the full row gateway. Its db/id/cents fields and exact parameter ordering cannot be removed by reuse.

entries.name: DAO — Data Access Object
entries.reason: DbDao and FixedDao deliberately differ and Service already shares one read call through the DAO. Sharing their few DATA fields with a template adds more code than it saves.

entries.name: DTO — Data Transfer Object
entries.reason: The DTO must copy exactly id and cents and omit token/methods. A generic merge or prefix copy would change the exported fields; a helper for two assignments is longer.

entries.name: Domain Model
entries.reason: One balance guard and one subtraction form the full domain operation. No repeated action exists within the example; the negative-amount and insufficient-funds paths remain explicit.

entries.name: Transaction Script
entries.reason: The two reads/writes target different accounts and are ordered inside a transaction. A generic transfer helper would merely relocate this whole implementation and need additional fields; atomic is already reused as the external transaction boundary.

entries.name: Table Module
entries.reason: The total loop occurs once and preserves rows. A complete reducer callback plus generic fold/result/error adaptation is longer than this small measured loop.

entries.name: Service Layer
entries.reason: body is already the shared load/debit/save sequence used by the transaction boundary. Another wrapper would add a layer without removing repeated code; port argument names remain because their DATA order is external.

entries.name: Identity Map
entries.reason: get already shares cache lookup and invokes load only on a miss. A memoize wrapper would need the same key and original-object identity policy and would not shorten this complete cache client.

entries.name: Lazy Load
entries.reason: A single load attempt uses a temporary so failure leaves loaded false, and successful zero is cached. A reused initializer cannot replace this persistent graph state; there is no duplicate action to extract.

entries.name: Query Object
entries.reason: One range validation and one parameterized query form the example. A general predicate or SQL helper would add code without removing the required minimum/maximum and placeholder order.

entries.name: Specification
entries.reason: SpecificationExample already reuses a measured operand implementation. The two predicates have different comparisons; a parameterized predicate helper would exceed the two one-line bodies.

entries.name: Value Object
entries.reason: Resolve the unchanged Money template path once into a local reference money, reused by both copy operations and merge. All cents/currency fields, both independent constructions and the differing currency case remain visible.
entries.before_code:
Demo:
    return: int
    run:
        throws: OperandArity
        import: MoneyLibrary\Equality
        @: first (copy(MoneyLibrary\immutable\Money))
        @: second (copy(MoneyLibrary\immutable\Money))
        @: third (merge(MoneyLibrary\immutable\Money; immutable: (int: currency 978)))
        return: (first equals second) * 10 + (first equals third)
entries.after_code:
Demo:
    return: int
    run:
        throws: OperandArity
        import: MoneyLibrary\Equality
        @: money MoneyLibrary\immutable\Money
        @: first (copy(money))
        @: second (copy(money))
        @: third (merge(money; immutable: (int: currency 978)))
        return: (first equals second) * 10 + (first equals third)

entries.name: Optimistic Offline Lock
entries.reason: One compare-and-set result check is already minimal. Sharing a Conflict helper would add a definition and call for one throw and cannot remove the version check.

entries.name: Pessimistic Offline Lock
entries.reason: acquire, save and release are different lease operations with different arities. A common wrapper would still require their full dispatch and token arguments; no duplicate behavior can be removed.

entries.name: Front Controller
entries.reason: Use the visible Front input order admitted, route in demo. Both authorization and unknown-route branches remain unchanged.
entries.before_code:
Front:
    int: admitted
    int: route
    return: int
    handle:
        if: admitted = 0
            return: 403
        if: route = 1
            return: 200
        return: 404
    demo:
        return: handle(admitted := 1; route := 1)
entries.after_code:
Front:
    int: admitted
    int: route
    return: int
    handle:
        if: admitted = 0
            return: 403
        if: route = 1
            return: 200
        return: 404
    demo:
        return: handle(1; 1)

entries.name: Page Controller
entries.reason: Use the sole visible quantity input in demo. The invalid-quantity branch and subtotal calculation remain unchanged.

OrderPage:
    int: quantity
    return: int
    handle:
        if: quantity < 1

        return: quantity * 10
    demo:

OrderPage:

entries.name: Application Controller
entries.reason: submit already shares validation and transition; valid follows the initialized screen field, so a bare positional 1 would select screen. A helper cannot shorten one conditional state update.

entries.name: Circuit Breaker
entries.reason: Resetting failures and until affects two different persistent fields. A complete reset helper or grouped assignment is longer, while the request/timeout and retry-count observations must remain.

entries.name: Retry
entries.reason: The client already uses the measured status-based retry operand once. Generic exception retry has a different contract and cannot replace 503 filtering plus backoff for free.

entries.name: Bulkhead
entries.reason: Acquire and release make different state transitions. A shared setter would need the requested state and return handling and is longer than the two tiny bodies; duplicate-acquire rejection remains.

entries.name: Saga
entries.reason: Factor the common phase write into the final action != 0 block. Each kind matches at most one transition branch, branch tests have no effects, and every original next phase equals action; phase is still committed before publishing exactly once.
entries.before_code:
SagaMessage:
    int: phase 0
    int: kind
    int: ok
    @: transport
    handle:
        int: action 0
        if: kind = 0 && node\phase = 0
            node\phase := 1
            action := 1
        if: kind = 1 && node\phase = 1
            if: ok
                node\phase := 2
                action := 2
            else:
                node\phase := 4
                action := 4
        ---
        if: kind = 2 && node\phase = 2
            if: ok
                node\phase := 5
                action := 5
            else:
                node\phase := 3
                action := 3
        ---
        if: kind = 3 && node\phase = 3 && ok
            node\phase := 4
            action := 4
        if: action != 0
            node\transport\publish(action)
entries.after_code:
SagaMessage:
    int: phase 0
    int: kind
    int: ok
    @: transport
    handle:
        int: action 0
        if: kind = 0 && node\phase = 0
            action := 1
        if: kind = 1 && node\phase = 1
            if: ok
                action := 2
            else:
                action := 4
        ---
        if: kind = 2 && node\phase = 2
            if: ok
                action := 5
            else:
                action := 3
        ---
        if: kind = 3 && node\phase = 3 && ok
            action := 4
        if: action != 0
            node\phase := action
            node\transport\publish(action)

entries.name: API Gateway
entries.reason: The two routes need distinct endpoints and paths, and an unknown route must make no HTTP call. A lookup table or post helper plus both entries is longer than the two guarded calls.

entries.name: Backends for Frontends
entries.reason: Mobile and Web are distinct Message boundaries with intentionally different provider call counts. Sharing backend DATA would merge those boundaries, while a template costs more than repeating the short declaration.

entries.name: Sidecar
entries.reason: Application post and sidecar sink write are different participants and effects. The external sidecar append input order is not locally fixed; no duplicate sender block exists here.

entries.name: Ambassador
entries.reason: The HTTP read method is already reused by the RetryLibrary operand. Both endpoint/route and status retry remain; another helper removes no repeated implementation.

entries.name: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
entries.reason: Use the sole visible quantity input for Checkout.total in demo. Legacy, conversion adapter and checkout remain separate and complete.
entries.before_code:
Legacy:
    return: int
    dollars:
        return: 12

ACL:
    return: int
    cents:
        return: Legacy\dollars() * 100

Checkout:
    int: quantity
    return: int
    total:
        return: quantity * ACL\cents()
    demo:
        return: total(quantity := 2)
entries.after_code:
Legacy:
    return: int
    dollars:
        return: 12

ACL:
    return: int
    cents:
        return: Legacy\dollars() * 100

Checkout:
    int: quantity
    return: int
    total:
        return: quantity * ACL\cents()
    demo:
        return: total(2)

entries.name: Strangler Fig
entries.reason: Use the visible Backends.route position, and set demo-local route to 1 once for two handle() calls via autofill. The final route 2 remains explicitly named; migrated state writes and response order remain 101,201,102.
entries.before_code:
Backends:
    int: route
    return: int
    legacy:
        return: 100 + route
    modern:
        return: 200 + route

Router:
    int: migrated 0
    int: route
    return: int
    handle:
        if: route = 1 && node\migrated != 0
            return: Backends\modern(route := route)
        return: Backends\legacy(route := route)
    demo:
        node\migrated := 0
        int: before handle(route := 1)
        node\migrated := 1
        return: before + handle(route := 1) + handle(route := 2)
entries.after_code:
Backends:
    int: route
    return: int
    legacy:
        return: 100 + route
    modern:
        return: 200 + route

Router:
    int: migrated 0
    int: route
    return: int
    handle:
        if: route = 1 && node\migrated != 0
            return: Backends\modern(route)
        return: Backends\legacy(route)
    demo:
        int: route 1
        node\migrated := 0
        int: before handle()
        node\migrated := 1
        return: before + handle() + handle(route := 2)

entries.name: Transactional Outbox
entries.reason: Write and relay already separate transaction and delivery. publish must precede markSent, including the crash window; there is no duplicate operation within either body that a complete helper removes.

entries.name: Cache-Aside
entries.reason: get loads once and put writes before invalidating. Sharing the ready flag updates would need distinct values and timing and adds a helper; the returned value and persistent cache remain.

entries.name: Materialized View
entries.reason: Reuse the existing query() for both apply return paths. Duplicate detection and Gap rejection remain before mutation, and successful total/last updates complete before query reads the total.
entries.before_code:
ProjectionMessage:
    int: total 0
    int: last 0
    int: seq
    int: delta
    return: int
    apply:
        throws: Gap
        if: seq <= node\last
            return: node\total
        if: seq != node\last + 1
            throw: Gap()
        node\total += delta
        node\last := seq
        return: node\total
    query:
        return: node\total
entries.after_code:
ProjectionMessage:
    int: total 0
    int: last 0
    int: seq
    int: delta
    return: int
    apply:
        throws: Gap
        if: seq <= node\last
            return: query()
        if: seq != node\last + 1
            throw: Gap()
        node\total += delta
        node\last := seq
        return: query()
    query:
        return: node\total

entries.name: Sharding
entries.reason: One guard and one selected target call form the sharding operation. length appears twice but a named count local would add more characters than it removes; target identity/order remains.

entries.name: Throttling
entries.reason: Window reset and per-request count increment are different state transitions. A generic counter helper must preserve boundary timing and adds more code than the repeated node paths.

entries.name: Queue-Based Load Leveling
entries.reason: There is only one pop/process sequence. Keeping the named next local preserves the caller context available to the external process callback; a new collection wrapper cannot remove repeated logic.

entries.name: Competing Consumers
entries.reason: Reuse WorkerMessage.start() after each successful process(job) instead of repeating its complete post/ask/answer block. The empty sentinel returns before processing or posting; queueOwner and explicit selfAddress continuation remain identical.
entries.before_code:
JobQueueMessage:
    @: queue
    return: int
    take:
        if: queue\size() = 0
            return: -1
        return: queue\pop()

WorkerMessage:
    int: job
    @: queueOwner
    @: selfAddress
    @: process
    start:
        post:
            ask:
                queueOwner\take()
            answer:
                selfAddress\received
    ---
    received:
        if: job = -1
            return
        process(job)
        post:
            ask:
                queueOwner\take()
            answer:
                selfAddress\received
entries.after_code:
JobQueueMessage:
    @: queue
    return: int
    take:
        if: queue\size() = 0
            return: -1
        return: queue\pop()

WorkerMessage:
    int: job
    @: queueOwner
    @: selfAddress
    @: process
    start:
        post:
            ask:
                queueOwner\take()
            answer:
                selfAddress\received
    ---
    received:
        if: job = -1
            return
        process(job)
        start()

entries.name: Leader Election
entries.reason: Acquire, fenced write and release are three different ordered external effects. A shared wrapper would only hide the same complete sequence and could change the zero-token early return.

entries.name: Health Endpoint Monitoring
entries.reason: live and ready deliberately differ: only ready probes the database. Sharing a status helper would add a callable around a single conditional and cannot erase the probe boundary.

entries.name: Claim Check
entries.reason: Ticket construction and payload checking belong to separate Message participants. Reusing a generic projection must still keep key/size fields, permissions and length validation; no shorter complete helper was established.

entries.name: Idempotent Consumer / Transactional Inbox
entries.reason: apply is already the single transaction callback. ACK must occur only after atomic returns; merging the steps or sharing with a transport helper would erase the transaction/ack boundary.

entries.name: Backpressure
entries.reason: Grant and offer change credits in opposite directions, and offer must post only with available credit. A shared update helper costs more and could obscure the no-send refusal path.

entries.name: Pipe — implementation
entries.reason: This is the measured implementation of the reused pipe operand. Replacing its sole loop with another hidden helper would remove the algorithm being compared rather than factor duplicated work.

entries.name: FindById — implementation
entries.reason: This measured search implementation has one arity check and one scan. A ready library search would cross the comparison boundary; first-duplicate identity and missing/empty behavior remain explicit.

entries.name: Specification combinator — implementation
entries.reason: The two captured predicate references and short-circuit call order are essential. No repeated executable body exists here; the copied owner and complete operand construction cannot be hidden in another helper.

entries.name: Money value equality — implementation
entries.reason: Equality must compare both cents and currency. A generic record comparison or shared field getter would add code or change the explicit value contract; both fields and the operand arity check remain.

entries.name: Retry Library — Implementation
entries.reason: RetryLibrary already implements a shared operation for two clients. One loop controls optional delay, status filtering and attempt limit; factoring its single-use guards/body into another helper grows the complete implementation.
